prompt: Which of the following describes all solutions to $3x - 5 > 10$?
hint: An inequality is solved with the same moves as an equation. Think about whether any of your moves will affect the direction of the sign.

hints.text: An inequality is solved with the same moves as an equation. Think about whether any of your moves will affect the direction of the sign.
Add $5$ to both sides to get $3x > 15$. Then divide by $3$, which is positive, so the sign keeps its direction.
Dividing $15$ by $3$ gives $x > 5$, which is choice A.

explanation: Add $5$ to both sides to isolate the $x$ term: $3x > 15$.
Divide both sides by $3$. Because $3$ is positive, the inequality keeps its direction: $x > 5$.
Test a value such as $x = 6$: $3(6) - 5 = 13$, which is greater than $10$. The solution is $x > 5$, choice A.

alternativeExplanations.title: Test a value to confirm the direction
steps: If you are unsure whether the answer is $x > 5$ or $x < 5$, test one number from each side.
One test settles the direction, and it takes five seconds.
